samples.summary: The new `setDocument() must not be called inside batch()` guard is instance-local (`this.activeRoot`), but a second `YorkieDocStore` is constructed over the same Yorkie document elsewhere and calls `setDocument` on it. That instance sees `activeRoot === null`, passes the guard, and opens a `doc.update` that could nest inside another instance's open batch update (which the diff's own `withUpdate` doc-comment says Yorkie does not support).
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:224 `new YorkieDocStore(doc).setDocument(content.document);` — a fresh store over the same `doc`; the guard added at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:796 only inspects the *calling* instance's `activeRoot`. Also packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/docs-scenarios.tsx / hunt page construct their own stores. Reachability across a live editor batch is unproven (import apply is async and the batch is synchronous), hence low confidence; the fix, if any, belongs on the guard (make it observe the shared doc's update state).

samples.summary: A throwing `YorkieDocStore.batch()` now rolls the whole `doc.update` back, but only the store's own cache is reset — `Doc._document` in packages/docs keeps the never-committed state. Before this change each write was its own `doc.update`, so partial writes really did land and the model cache matched reality.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:99 `private _document: Document;` refreshed only via `refresh()` (line 123). Inside `withNamedStyleChange` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1081) `doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll()` calls `refresh()` and caches the post-write document; if the batch then throws, `YorkieDocStore.batch`'s finally sets `dirty = true; cachedDoc = null` but nothing tells `Doc` to re-read, so subsequent edits compute offsets from a document Yorkie discarded. Fix belongs on the new batch/`withNamedStyleChange` path (refresh the model on the throw path).

samples.summary: `skipNonHistoryPresence()` silently turns `setCursorForHistory`'s presence flush into a no-op inside a batch, which would make undo restore a stale/collapsed selection for any caller composed into a batch. No current caller is inside a batch, but the memory-store comments explicitly anticipate composing whole editor operations inside one, and the `DocStore.batch` contract does not warn about it.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3022-3027 `setCursorForHistory` → `this.updateCursorPos(pos, selection ?? null)`, documented as the synchronous pre-edit presence flush that Yorkie captures as reverse presence; `updateCursorPos` now early-returns inside a batch (line ~3151). Callers at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1031, 1140, 1985, 2194, 3040 are all currently outside batches. Slides folds presence into the ambient proxy instead of dropping it (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:2743).

samples.summary: `YorkieDocStore.setDocument()` now throws inside a batch, but `MemDocStore.setDocument()` has no such guard and the `DocStore.batch()` contract in store.ts does not list the restriction. Code written and tested against the memory store (the docs package's only store) would pass and throw only under the collaborative store.

verdict.reason: The claimed "second YorkieDocStore over the same Yorkie document" does not exist. At apply-imported-content.ts:220 the Document is constructed fresh inside the function (`new Document<YorkieDocsRoot>(docKey)`), attached to its own Client activated at line 203 and detached at line 225; the store built at line 224 is the only store ever wrapping that object, so its `doc.update` cannot nest inside any other instance's batch (Yorkie update state is per-Document-instance; only the server docKey is shared, not the in-memory object). A repo-wide Grep for `YorkieDocStore` in packages/frontend/src finds exactly two construction sites — docs-view.tsx:324 (one store per mounted doc, held in storeRef, whose setDocument call at docs-view.tsx:356 is at the top of the mount effect, outside any batch) and apply-imported-content.ts:224 — so no Document is wrapped by two stores. The other cited sites do not construct Yorkie stores at all: harness/visual/docs-scenarios.tsx:108-109 and harness/hunt/page.tsx:503-504 both use `new MemDocStore()`, an in-memory store with no doc.update. Finally, the guard's stated purpose (yorkie-doc-store.ts:790-798) is that `undoFloor` reads the undo stack after the write, which is an instance-local coupling, not the cross-instance nesting the finding posits.

verdict.reason: No counterexample exists. `Doc` caches the document in `_document` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:99,105) and only re-reads it via `refresh()` (line 123); the getter at line 108 does no lazy read. `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` (lines 515-534) refreshes on entry and after its write, so mid-batch state is cached. `withNamedStyleChange` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1080-1092) is the sole `docStore.batch()` call site in packages/docs/src and has no try/catch/finally, so a throw escapes before any refresh/render. `YorkieDocStore.batch`'s non-commit `finally` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2881-2889) resets only `dirty`/`cachedDoc`. I checked every `.refresh()` call site in the repo for a recovery path: docs-view.tsx:380 sits inside `store.onRemoteChange`, which only fires on Yorkie `remote-change` events (yorkie-doc-store.ts:599-604) and so is not triggered by a locally rolled-back update; editor.ts:3703 (`resetAfterDocumentReplace`) is reached only from the DOCX-import path (docs-view.tsx:352-369). editor.ts contains no catch on the style paths. So after a throw the model cache holds writes Yorkie discarded, and nothing tells it to re-read. Impact is narrower than the write-up implies (this batch is style-only, so text offsets do not shift, and the divergence self-heals on the next mutation's own refresh), but the store/model incoherence is real, reachable, and the fix belongs on the new batch path.
